messages.subject: Doubts regarding Rserve and JRI
messages.subject_clean: Doubts regarding Rserve and JRI
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've been working for a while with Rserve and it is just great. Nevertheless, a few things are still a little bit confusing to me.
My goal is to develop a Java application that will allow the users to use R, eventually remotely. In this development there are two main problems:

1. Convert Java objects into R objects. This is working fine using REngine (RConnection when remotly) and the REXP* classes and the REXPWrapper.
2. Convert the result R objects into Java data structures. By now, what I'm doing is to use the REngine.eval to execute whatever command the user has typed, and then I've created a kind of "decision tree" (a bunch of ifs) that evaluate the type of object obtained with R (using asInteger, asString, asList, ...) to decide how to transform such output into a Java object.

Is this the right way to do so? Which is the best way to create Java objects from R objects?

Tahnk you very much for your help.

Víctor

Great, this is really useful.
However, while inspecting the output of REXP.asNativeJavaObject I've noticed that in some cases it returns 100% Java native data structures, while in some others returns RServe Objects.

For instance:

While "a <- c(1,2,5.3,6,-2,4)" returns a list of doubles (not a REXPDouble), and b <- "hello" returns a String, "mydata <- data.frame(a, b)" returns a RList filled with a REXPInteger that contains a number 3 and a REXPFactor containing the string "hello". In a similar example "mylist <- list(a, b)" returns again a RList with again a REXPInteger and a REXPString. Is that correct, or can be considered as a bug?

Hope that helps to test the REXP.asNativeJavaObject method.
Thank you for your help.

Víctor

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Are there size limits for the REXP object returned by parseAndEval ? I have an analysis that returns the object fine when a parameter is set so that there are 26000 rows in the data frame. But when the parameter is different, and there are 3080420 rows, I get 0 rows returned to Java.

My code is :

REXP result = RPanel.rExec.parseAndEval("final <- aFunction(x, y, z)");
PrintWriter pw = new PrintWriter(new FileOutputStream("resLen.txt"));
pw.print("nRows=" + result.asList().at(0).length());

I ran the code with the same parameters in R, to confirm it's not a different parameter that's causing the problem in the R code. The data frame is created fine in a standalone R session. I'd love to avoid doing it in chunks and looping and appending in Java.

Thanks,
       Dario.

--------------------------------------
Dario Strbenac
Research Assistant
Cancer Epigenetics
Garvan Institute of Medical Research
Darlinghurst NSW 2010

messages.subject: Re: how are NA's moved by rJava
messages.subject_clean: how are NA's moved by rJava
messages.body_plain:
The quick answer is that NAs are passed exactly as they are represented in R, rJava doesn't do any special processing on them. So if you know how NAs are represented in R, you're done ;)

On Jan 8, 2012, at 6:42 PM, Adrian Dragulescu wrote:

> 
> Hello,
> 
> Say I have a character array
> A <- .jarray(c("A", NA, "B"))
> and I pass it to a java method that expects a String[], how can I test that the second value is NA?.
> 

This is a bit tricky, because in R NAs are simply a string "NA" so currently you can't really distinguish NA from "NA".


> Same question for a numeric array, with a double[]
> N <- .jarray(c(1.0, NA, 2.0))
> How can I test inside my java method for NA?
> 

R represents NAs as special NaNs with the bits 0x7ff00000000007a2L. See org.rosuda.REngine.REXPDouble.isNA() for determining NAs.


> And for int[]?
> 

NA is -2147483648 - again, see org.rosuda.REngine.REXPInteger.isNA() but this one is more trivial.


> I couldn't find it in the docs or the list.  I can probably figure it out, but if it takes somebody only one minute to reply, even better.
> 

Thanks for showing us how little you value our time :P.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Unlinked Exception Even With LD_LIBRARY_PATH set
messages.subject_clean: Unlinked Exception Even With LD_LIBRARY_PATH set
messages.body_plain:
On Jan 12, 2012, at 9:00 PM, Dario Strbenac wrote:

> Hi again,
> 
> I'm testing out my plugin in Ubuntu now. As can be seen in the output, my LD_LIBRARY_PATH is set, but when I run my code I get an Unsatisfied Link Error from exc.getMessage()
> 
> darstr@clark-lab:~$ echo $LD_LIBRARY_PATH
> /home/darstr/R/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-library/2.13/rJava/jri/libjri.so:/usr/local/lib64/R/lib/libR.so
> 

That is wrong - LD_LIBRARY_PATH lists *directories* to look up in so what you probably meant was

export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/darstr/R/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-library/2.13/rJava/jri:/usr/local/lib64/R/lib



> darstr@clark-lab:~$ ls -l /home/darstr/R/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-library/2.13/rJava/jri/libjri.so
> -rwxr-xr-x 1 darstr darstr 163021 2012-01-12 09:31 /home/darstr/R/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-library/2.13/rJava/jri/libjri.so
> darstr@clark-lab:~$ ls -l /usr/local/lib64/R/lib/libR.so
> -rwxr-xr-x 1 root root 9322029 2011-05-18 13:24 /usr/local/lib64/R/lib/libR.so
> 
> Cannot find JRI native library!
> Please make sure that the JRI native library is in a directory listed in java.library.path.
> 
> Anything more needed ?
> 

Well, the message really tells you that the canonical way is to use the java.library.path setting - it inherits from LD_LIBRARY_PATH so it doesn't matter whichever you use, but a typical JRI application is started with

R CMD java -Djava.library.path=.../rJava/jri -jar myApp.jar

which takes care of everything needed.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Daniel,

On Jan 27, 2012, at 10:19 AM, Daniel Chapsky wrote:

> Hi all ,
> 
> 
> Does anybody have any insight to how control commands might be implemented from the R client for Rserve? So far I've tried implementing CMD_ctrlEval command from the QAP1 protocol by altering the current RSeval code thusly:
> 
> RSevalControl <- function(c, expr) {
> 	r <- if (is.character(expr)) serialize(parse(text=paste("{",paste(expr,collapse="\n"),"}"))[[1]],NULL) else serialize(expr, NULL)
> 	writeBin(c(0x42L, length(r), 0L, 0L), c, endian="little")
> 	writeBin(r, c)
>        
> 	##b <- readBin(c,"int",4,endian="little") # the return lines commented out because I dont' think the control commands are supposed to return anything
> }
> 
> Anybody have any pointers on how I could get this working?
> 

The R client cheats and completely bypasses the regular protocol used by Rserve and uses R serialization installed, so you can't use it with "regular" Rserve commands (like CMD_ctrlEval).

However, in the special case if CMD_ctrlEval you don't need any transcoding of R objects, so it's actually not that hard to implement - it is in fact exactly the same format as RSlogin except for the command code. I have added RSserverEval and RSserverSource to Rserve 0.6-8.

Cheers,
Simon
